Nurturing today's readers, inspiring tomorrow's leaders
Key Staff
Welcome to Twynham Primary School
Welcome to Twynham Primary School. We hope you find everything you are looking for.
We are currently a single form entry primary school with children from Year R to Year 6 situated in West Christchurch.

Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Twynham Primary School — a place where every child is known, valued and inspired to flourish. We are proud of our caring, ambitious community and of the shared belief that education is about far more than academic success alone. At TPS, we work together to nurture confident learners, thoughtful citizens and kind human beings who are prepared for the opportunities and challenges of the wider world.
Central to our vision is a deep commitment to nurturing today’s readers. We recognise that literacy is the gateway to learning, creativity and independence, and is fundamental to equity and social justice. By fostering a genuine love for reading and providing tailored support, we empower children to become confident, capable readers who can access knowledge, express themselves clearly and develop empathy and understanding for others. We believe that strong literacy opens doors — academically, socially and emotionally — and remains a lifelong gift.
Alongside this, we are dedicated to inspiring tomorrow’s leaders. Leadership at TPS is not about titles or positions; it is about responsibility, integrity and having the confidence to make positive choices. We encourage children to take ownership of their learning, to show humility and respect, and to recognise that they can make a difference — within school, in their community and beyond. Through purposeful opportunities for leadership, collaboration and reflection, our pupils develop the skills and values they will need to thrive in an ever‑changing world.
Everything we do is guided by our STAR values, which shine brightly across our school and shape the character of our community.
Service sits at the heart of our ethos. We instil in our pupils a strong sense of responsibility to others, encouraging acts of kindness, empathy and contribution so that giving back becomes a natural part of who they are.
Aspiration drives our high expectations. We inspire children to dream big, work hard and persevere, supporting them to achieve their full potential while celebrating effort as much as outcome.
Respect underpins our relationships. We nurture a culture where difference is celebrated, voices are listened to and every individual is treated with dignity and care.
Teamwork defines how we work and learn together. As Team TPS, pupils, staff and families collaborate in partnership, valuing each other’s strengths and working towards shared goals.
At Twynham Primary School, children grow not only in knowledge but in confidence, compassion and character. We are immensely proud of our school and warmly invite you to become part of our journey, as together we prepare our children for a future filled with purpose, contribution and fulfilment.
I hope that you find the information contained on this website useful.
If you have any further questions, please do not hesitate to contact the school office: office@twynhamprimary.com
Mrs Jennifer HunterHeadteacher

SEND & Wellbeing News
TPS COFFEE MORNINGS
We are pleased to invite parents and carers to join us for one of our School Coffee Mornings.
These informal gatherings are a lovely opportunity to come along, enjoy a hot drink and biscuit, and have a relaxed chat with members of our staff team.
The coffee mornings provide a welcoming space for parents and carers to:
There is no formal agenda — just an opportunity to come together, have a chat and share ideas in a friendly and relaxed environment.
We would love to see you there!
Share ideas, knowledge and experiences.
Ask questions and chat informally with staff.
EMOTION COACHING SESSIONS
At TPS we use Emotion Coaching to support our children and aid re-regulation. This hour long information session is designed to support parent understanding of Emotion Coaching and ways the strategies can be used at home too.
SEND PROVISION UPDATE FROM BCP
We are pleased to share that the Department for Education has recognised the positive progress being made to improve support for children and young people with SEND across Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole.
As a result, the government has stepped down its statutory direction for the BCP SEND Local Area Partnership to an Improvement Notice. This reflects growing confidence in the work taking place across education, health and care services to strengthen support for children and young people with SEND.
This is an important milestone and recognises the collective efforts of schools, settings, partners, children, young people and families who have worked together to drive improvements across the local area. We would like to thank everyone who has contributed to this progress.
While we welcome this recognition, we know that improvement is an ongoing journey. We recognise that some children, young people and families continue to face challenges, and that not everyone will yet have experienced the positive changes being made. We remain committed to ensuring that improvements are felt consistently by all those who rely on SEND services and support.
The move to an Improvement Notice acknowledges the progress that has been made so far and provides encouragement that we are moving in the right direction. At the same time, it reinforces the importance of continuing to build on this progress and embed lasting improvements across the local area. Our focus remains on delivering better experiences and outcomes for children and young people with SEND.
The voices of children, young people, parents and carers will continue to be at the heart of this work. Your experiences, feedback and insights are invaluable in helping us understand what is working well and where we can do better. By continuing to work together, we can build on the foundations already in place and shape services that better meet the needs of local families.
Thank you to all parents and carers who continue to share their experiences and help shape local SEND services. Your feedback plays a vital role in our ongoing improvement work, and we remain committed to listening, learning and working in partnership with you as we continue this journey

STORMBREAK SHINE
Stormbreak Shine pathways are short (between 15 and 30 minute) sessions, which can be followed at home to help support a range of needs.
If you would like further information or to have access to any of the pathways below, please email senco@twynhamprimary.com, stating your child(ren)’s name and which pathway(s) you would like more information/access to
FACE TRAINING SESSIONS
Twynham Primary School has purchased a 12 month FACE Membership to allow parents access to all FACE training sessions (usually £24), free of charge.
There are 16 regular talks, which are on a four-weekly rotation, and can be accessed here. Please see the March timetable below.
Please see email for full details on how to book.
Links to recordings of the talks are available for 48 hours after the session. If you cannot make the live session, book on and then email info@facefamilyadvice.co.uk to request the recording link.
STORMBREAK AT TPS
We have recently launched Stormbreak at Twynham Primary School.
Stormbreak is a charity (registered in England and Wales) that supports young children’s mental health through movement, equipping them with sustainable skills and coping strategies to thrive during the complex demands of growth into adult life.
Each Stormbreak lasts between 5 to 15 minutes and involves movement and associated conversation and discussion around mental health. At school, we use a mixture of pre-recorded videos and stormbreaks which are delivered by our school staff.
Stormbreak is something that can also be completed at home, as a family, and this PDF contains all the information you should need. It is easy to set up your own parent account, and this video explains how to do it.

Art & Design
Our aim at Twynham Primary School is to enable pupils to become creative and reflective learners who are able to express themselves fluently and confidently in a variety of different ways. Within our curriculum, Art and Design will regularly contribute towards this by enabling pupils to respond thoughtfully to different learning and stimuli. Throughout their time at TPS, our young artists should be able to develop their cultural understanding in a range of contexts, Art being one of them.
We value Art and Design as an important part of the children’s entitlement to a broad and balanced curriculum. Art and Design provides the children with the opportunities to develop and extend skills and an opportunity to express their individual interests, thoughts and ideas.
Art, craft and design embody some of the highest forms of human creativity. A high-quality art and design education should engage, inspire and challenge pupils, equipping them with the knowledge and skills to experiment, invent and create their own works of art, craft and design. As pupils progress, they should be able to think critically and develop a more rigorous understanding of art and design. They should also know how art and design both reflect and shape our history, and contribute to the culture, creativity and wealth of our world.
As with all our primary subjects, the Twynham Learning Primary Curriculum Intent drives the children’s ambitious and engaging learning journey.
Art and Design Overview

With an increased emphasis on Computing in a technologically developed world, we feel that it is important that children learn to use and understand the electronics at their disposal.
With this in mind, every year group covers units in Computing alongside units in e-safety, which is, of course, a priority as the children become more familiar with the internet.

pageCache.pageTitle: Twynham Primary School - Report an absent child
pageCache.text:
Report an absent child
If your child is unwell, please inform us by telephone 01202 026065 on the first day of absence and by no later than 9:30am.
If your child remains unwell then we ask that you telephone the school again on the third day of absence and that you keep us informed.
If you know in advance that your child needs to be absent (e.g. for a medical or dental appointment) then please do let us know by contacting the school in advance of the appointment.

Booking and Registering
Wraparound Childcare
Children can be dropped off by parents any time from the start of the session, this is typically 7:30am and staff will ensure children arrive at their class ready to learn at the start of the school day.
Breakfast includes items such as a selection of cereals, toast, crumpets, milk, water and fruit.
In the course of a session children have access to the outdoor areas, IT equipment and the opportunity to catch up on reading and homework. There will be a range of art and craft activities available.
A cold evening snack will be available to those children whose parents have pre-booked. These snacks will range from pizza, sandwiches and wraps which are all cooked on site freshly each day.
Children of staff employed by the Trust and families with multiple children are entitled to a 5% discount as detailed below. Please note that the maximum discount is 5%.
ONLY AVAILABLE WHEN BOOKING AFTER SCHOOL 2
Please ensure that your child is picked up promptly. We recommend that you arrive 5 minutes before the end of session to ensure that your child is picked up on time.
The after school club must close at 6pm every evening, so you need to have picked your child up and left the premises by this time.
We reserve the right to charge for attendance outside the agreed hours. If late collection is persistent, we will charge £10 for late collections.

British Values
At Twynham Primary we recognise our obligation to promote and teach the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.

Firstly, we would like to welcome you to Twynham Primary School, the start of your child's educational journey.
We know that there are lots of questions you must have and so we have consolidated everything we think you need to know on our website, so that you can access it whenever you need it, wherever you are.
Below are some of the key information pages and key dates but please do spend some time on our site to understand our curriculum and other important aspects of our school. In particular, can we please draw your attention to the school uniform.
Please note that Reception year starts on a part-time basis for the first week of the new school year in September. An email will be sent to all parents to confirm whether your child will attend the morning or afternoon sessions during the settling in period.

Foundation Subjects
Please click on the links detailed for more information on our Foundation Subjects

Maths
In Maths, we follow the Maths No Problem curriculum across all year groups. More information about how this works, along with information on our mastery curriculum, can be found by clicking here. The Maths No Problem blog, containing lots of useful information for parents, can be found here.
The Maths curriculum is broken down into strands and these are gradually built upon so that children and parents alike can clearly see the progress being made.

Music Tuition
In addition to our high-quality whole-class music lessons, we are able to offer children in Years 3-6 the opportunity to learn to play an instrument. We value music highly at Twynham Primary School, working closely with the Twynham School Music Department to provide highly skilled peripatetic music teachers.
There are many benefits to learning a musical instrument – coordination, memory, resilience and perseverance, to name but a few, as well as laying the foundations for a lifetime of enjoying playing music. Starting to learn an instrument at a young age is particularly beneficial.
If you would like to discuss any aspect of music tuition, please feel free to come into school, or contact the school office here.

Music
At Twynham Primary, we pride ourselves on our Music Curriculum, which sees the children learn songs and use skills closely related to their topic activities in the classroom. We have a qualified music specialist who leads music in all classes across the week.
We feel it is very important that children experience a range of instruments and styles of music across the year to give them the opportunity to find out what they enjoy.
Music Curriculum Overview
For more information, please contact the School Office.

Reading
At Twynham Primary we understand that reading and writing are fundamental skills that enable our children to access other areas of the curriculum as well as acquire a new hobby and a love of books that could last a lifetime. For more information on how reading and phonics are taught in school, please see the 'Reading and Phonics' link below.
